reason: Conversation 1 reached the correct conclusion quickly: the 9kg load exceeds the 6kg dry capacity and the spin was turned down to 800, so it confirmed the half-load test and advised splitting loads, with no part recommended. Its opening line about electrical tests being unsafe and calling a technician was unnecessary, and the closing did not restate the 'split loads and use full spin' advice explicitly. Conversation 2 acknowledged the heater works and the overload, but then sent the customer on a long filter and condenser hunt, including unplugging, unscrewing the pump filter and pulling out a 'condenser' it wrongly said was reachable behind the flap. It never settled on the overload and spin cause even after the half-drum test came out dry, so it was less efficient and gave questionable model-specific claims.
